Reported precision-recall AUC (average precision) at the sample prevalence

Source: R/fn_average_precision.R
pr_auc.Rd

Average precision computed at the evaluation sample's own prevalence – the ordinary (unweighted) PR-AUC a model reports from its test set, and the precision-side sibling of the prevalence-invariant roc_auc. It is exactly ap_pointwise evaluated at pi = mean(truth == 1) (where the prevalence weights become uniform); use ap_pointwise directly to re-price average precision to a different target prevalence.

Usage

pr_auc(truth, prob)

Arguments

truth

Outcomes coded 1 (presence) / 0 (absence).

prob

Predicted probabilities or scores, same length as truth.

Value

Scalar average precision at the sample prevalence, or NA_real_ if a class is absent.

Note

Unlike roc_auc, average precision is not inflated by easy absences, which is why it is the recommended anchor for curve reconstruction. This function is still a per-sample diagnostic: to rebuild a prevalence-corrected decision curve, pass the reported value – together with the prevalence it was measured at – to ap_scalar_to_prev or nb_binormal_band.

See also

roc_auc (the discrimination diagnostic), ap_pointwise (re-price to a target prevalence), ap_scalar_to_prev, nb_binormal_band.
